newsitem.title: USA: Dart Group extends CEO buyout settlement.
newsitem.headline: Dart Group extends CEO buyout settlement.

text.p: Dart Group Corp. said Tuesday it extended by 20 days the conditional settlement agreement in principle reached April 21 on a buyout for its chairman and chief executive, Herbert Haft.
Haft had agreed to a $42 million cash buyout in April to give up control of the multimillion dollar retail empire he founded.

Dart filed for bankruptcy in 1995 after a four-year-long feud among family members for control of the Landover, Md.-based company, which includes Crown Books Corp., Trak Auto Corp. and Shoppers Food Warehouse Corp.
The conditional agreement in principle had originally been due to expire if it did not become definitive by May 9, Dart said. That date was extended to May 23.
Dart and Haft have still not entered into a definitive settlement, and the agreement in principle has been amended to expire if a definitive agreement is not reached by June 12, Dart said.
"The parties are having difficulty resolving outstanding issues in the negotiations," a statement issued by Dart said.
Dart's stock fell $2.50 to $104.50 early on Nasdaq.
